headline: Why Your Kitchen Plumbing Upgrade Needs a Pro's Touch
articleBody:
Thinking about upgrading your kitchen plumbing? It's more than just picking out a new faucet! Relocating sinks, dishwashers, or even adding a pot filler can get complex pretty fast. These changes often require new supply or drain-waste-vent work, and that can trigger permit requirements you might not expect.

**What Can Change the Right Choice**
Choosing whether to DIY or hire a pro really depends on the scope. A simple faucet swap in the same spot? Probably fine. But if you’re moving any fixtures, extending water lines, altering drain piping, or especially if gas piping is involved, that’s when a qualified plumber becomes absolutely essential. Local rules dictate who can perform and certify this kind of work, and you don’t want to mess around with that.

**Common Mistakes to Avoid**
One common pitfall is treating an appliance replacement as purely cosmetic without considering the plumbing implications. Another big one is closing up walls before the rough-in inspection. You also need to ensure shutoffs are accessible and plan for cabinet clearances. Don't finalize plumbing plans before you've locked in your appliance and cabinet specifications – it’ll save you a lot of headaches down the line.

**When Professional Guidance Helps**
Any time you’re opening walls or floors, dealing with drain or vent alterations, or have water pressure issues, a professional is a must. They handle the tricky stuff like permit acquisition, ensuring everything meets code, and proper pressure and leak testing.
